nodes.summary: For a context $\Gamma$ and a type $A$, a certified canonical term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ together with a proof that $t$ is a fixed point of normalization by evaluation: the term underlying the normal form computed for $t$ is $t$ itself.
nodes.title: Certified canonical terms

nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a context, $A$ a type, and $\Gamma, A$ the context $\Gamma$ extended by a newest variable of type $A$. Transport the identity semantic environment of $\Gamma$ (which reflects each variable as a neutral value) along the weakening renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma, A$ that sends each variable to its successor, and extend the result by the reflection at type $A$ of the newest variable of $\Gamma, A$.…
nodes.title: The identity environment under a binder

nodes.summary: Given a semantic value $a$ of type $A$ in a context $\Delta$ and a semantic environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$ in $\Delta$, the extended environment is the semantic environment for the context $A :: \Gamma$ (the context $\Gamma$ with a new innermost variable of type $A$) in $\Delta$ that sends the new innermost variable to $a$ and sends the successor of each variable $x$ of $\Gamma$ to $\eta(x)$.
nodes.title: Extending a semantic environment by one variable

nodes.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types and an environment $\eta$ for a context $\Gamma$ in $I$. Then the identity Kripke semantic environment on $\Gamma$, which reflects each variable as a neutral value, realizes $\eta$ at $\eta$.
nodes.title: The identity semantic environment realizes every environment

nodes.summary: For a context $\Gamma$, the identity environment is the semantic environment for $\Gamma$ in $\Gamma$ that sends each variable $x$ of type $A$ to the reflection at type $A$ of the neutral term $x$. Reflection turns a neutral term into a semantic value of the same type in the same context.
nodes.title: The identity semantic environment

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$. If $t$ is canonical, then there is exactly one beta-normal, eta-long normal form of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ whose underlying term is $t$.
nodes.title: Canonical terms have a unique normal form

nodes.summary: A term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is canonical if and only if normalization by evaluation maps $t$ to itself, that is, the term underlying the normal form computed for $t$ is $t$.
nodes.title: Canonical terms are the fixed points of normalization

nodes.summary: For every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, the term obtained by normalizing $t$ by evaluation is canonical.
nodes.title: Normalized terms are canonical

nodes.summary: A term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is canonical when it is the underlying term of some beta-normal, eta-long normal form of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$.
nodes.title: Canonical terms

nodes.summary: If two terms $t$ and $u$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ have the same NbE normal form, then $t$ and $u$ are model-equal.
nodes.title: Equal NbE normal forms imply model equality

nodes.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types, contexts $\Delta$ and $\Gamma$, an environment $\theta$ for $\Delta$ in $I$, a Kripke semantic environment $\xi$ assigning to each variable of $\Gamma$ a semantic value in $\Delta$, and an environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$ in $I$. Then $\xi$ realizes $\eta$ at $\theta$ when for every type $A$ and every variable $x$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the semantic value $\xi(x)$…
nodes.title: Realization of environments

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, and let $\xi$ and $\zeta$ be semantic environments interpreting the variables of $\Gamma$ in a context $\Delta$. If $\xi(x) = \zeta(x)$ for every variable $x$ of $\Gamma$, of any type, then evaluating $t$ in $\xi$ and evaluating $t$ in $\zeta$ give the same semantic value.
nodes.title: Evaluation respects pointwise equal environments

nodes.summary: For every neutral term $n$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, evaluating the underlying term of $n$ in the identity semantic environment of $\Gamma$ gives the reflection of $n$ at type $A$.
nodes.title: Evaluating a neutral term reflects it

nodes.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types. Let $t$ be a term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, let $\xi$ be a Kripke semantic environment assigning to each variable of $\Gamma$ a semantic value in context $\Delta$, and let $\eta$ and $\theta$ be environments in $I$ for $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$. If $\xi$ realizes $\eta$ at $\theta$, then the NbE evaluation of $t$ in $\xi$ realizes the denotation of $t$ in $\eta$ at…
nodes.title: Fundamental lemma for NbE evaluation

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a term of type $T$ in context $\Gamma$ and let $\eta$ be a semantic environment interpreting every variable of $\Gamma$ as a semantic value in context $\Delta$. The evaluation $\operatorname{ev}(t, \eta)$ is the semantic value of type $T$ in context $\Delta$ defined by recursion on $t$: a variable $x$ evaluates to $\eta(x)$; an application $f\,a$ evaluates to the semantic function…
nodes.title: Evaluation into the Kripke semantic domain

nodes.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types. For a context $\Gamma$, an environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$ in $I$, a type $A$, a Kripke semantic value $v$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$ and an element $d$ of the denotation of $A$ under $I$, the relation "$v$ realizes $d$ at $\eta$" is defined by recursion on $A$. At a base type, $v$ is a neutral term, and $v$ realizes $d$ when the denotation of $v$, read as a term, in $\eta$…
nodes.title: Kripke realization relation for NbE

nodes.summary: For every beta-normal, eta-long normal form $n$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, normalizing the underlying term of $n$ by evaluation returns the normal form $n$ itself.
nodes.title: Normal forms are fixed points of normalization

nodes.summary: For a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, its normal form is the beta-normal, eta-long term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ obtained by reifying, at type $A$, the evaluation of $t$ in the identity semantic environment of $\Gamma$, which interprets each variable as the reflection of that variable.
nodes.title: Normalization by evaluation

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types, every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ and every environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$ in $I$, the NbE normal form of $t$ has the same denotation in $\eta$ as $t$.
nodes.title: NbE preserves denotation

nodes.summary: For every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, normalizing the normalized term of $t$ by evaluation gives the normalized term of $t$ again.
nodes.title: Normalization by evaluation is idempotent

nodes.summary: Every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is model-equal to its NbE normal form.
nodes.title: Every term is model-equal to its NbE normal form

nodes.summary: For every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, normalizing the underlying term of the normal form that normalization by evaluation computes from $t$ gives the same term as normalizing $t$.
nodes.title: Renormalizing a computed normal form

nodes.summary: For every interpretation $I$ of the base types and every term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, $t$ and its NbE normal form are semantically equal in $I$: they have the same denotation in every environment for $\Gamma$ in $I$.
nodes.title: Every term is semantically equal to its NbE normal form in each model

nodes.summary: For every eta-long normal form $n$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, normalizing the underlying term of $n$ returns that term unchanged.
nodes.title: Normalization fixes the terms of normal forms

nodes.summary: For a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, its normalized term is the term of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ underlying the beta-normal, eta-long normal form of $t$ computed by normalization by evaluation.
nodes.title: Normalization of terms

nodes.summary: For every type $A$, every renaming $\rho$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, and every neutral term $n$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, transporting the semantic value obtained by reflecting $n$ at type $A$ along $\rho$ gives the reflection at type $A$ of the neutral term $n$ renamed by $\rho$.
nodes.title: Reflection commutes with renaming

nodes.summary: Given a renaming $\rho$ from a context $\Delta$ to a context $\Theta$ and a semantic environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$ in $\Delta$, the renamed environment is the semantic environment for $\Gamma$ in $\Theta$ that sends each variable $x$ of type $A$ to the semantic value $\eta(x)$ renamed along $\rho$ at type $A$.
nodes.title: Renaming a semantic environment

nodes.summary: If a term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is canonical, then for every renaming $\rho$ from $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, the term obtained by renaming $t$ along $\rho$ is canonical.
nodes.title: Renaming preserves canonical terms

nodes.summary: Fix an interpretation $I$ of the base types. Let $v$ be a Kripke semantic value of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ that realizes an element $d$ of the denotation of $A$ at an environment $\eta$ for $\Gamma$. If $\rho : \Gamma \to \Delta$ is a renaming and $\theta$ is an environment for $\Delta$ with $\theta \circ \rho = \eta$, then the transport of $v$ along $\rho$ realizes $d$ at $\theta$.
nodes.title: Realization is stable under renaming

nodes.summary: Given a renaming $\rho$ from a context $\Gamma$ to a context $\Delta$, a simple type $A$ and a semantic value $v$ of type $A$ in $\Gamma$, the renamed value is the semantic value of type $A$ in $\Delta$ defined by cases on $A$. At a base type it is the neutral term $v$ with its free variables renamed by $\rho$. At an arrow type $A = B \Rightarrow C$ it sends a renaming $\sigma$ from $\Delta$ to a context $\Theta$…
nodes.title: Renaming a semantic value

nodes.summary: For contexts $\Delta$ and $\Gamma$, a semantic environment for $\Gamma$ in $\Delta$ assigns to every variable of $\Gamma$, of any type $A$, a Kripke semantic value of type $A$ in $\Delta$.
nodes.title: Semantic environments for normalization by evaluation

nodes.summary: For a context $\Gamma$, the semantic values of a simple type in $\Gamma$ are defined by recursion on the type. At a base type $b$ they are the neutral terms of type $b$ in $\Gamma$ (variables applied to zero or more normal arguments). At an arrow type $A \Rightarrow B$ a semantic value is a family that, for every context $\Delta$ and every renaming from $\Gamma$ to $\Delta$, maps semantic values of type $A$ in…
nodes.title: Kripke semantic values

nodes.summary: The canonical term of an eta-long normal form $n$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ is the underlying term of $n$, certified to be a fixed point of normalization.
nodes.title: Normal forms as canonical terms

nodes.summary: For a canonical term $t$ of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$, that is, a term that normalization returns unchanged, its normal form is the eta-long normal form that normalization by evaluation computes from $t$.
nodes.title: The normal form of a canonical term

nodes.summary: For every context $\Gamma$ and type $A$, two eta-long normal forms of type $A$ in context $\Gamma$ with the same underlying term are equal.
nodes.title: Erasing normal forms is injective

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
